title: review: R14a v3: jev_route active ranking (Phase I P5) — bounded Jev suitability adjustment on hypothetical()'s single favoured executor, shrunk by a shared per-class sample count; cold start and failure reproduce baseline
spec:
Why: [jev.routing].mode accepts "active" but jev_route.shadow_context (orchestrator/jev_route.py:165-176) only emits a notify() stub; hypothetical() (146-163) is the shadow heuristic. Phase I P5 requires active mode to modify ranking among eligible candidates as candidate_score = configured_weight x empirical_score x jev_suitability_adjustment, with extreme probabilities unable to overwhelm strong empirical evidence, cold start safe, failure reproducing baseline. v3 after spec reviews T-0590 and T-0604.
What (the executor.start hook that feeds adjusted scores into pool.pick_executor is a later integration task). Tests are unittest.TestCase methods in the named files.
- scorecard.py: extract the resolved-task filter of class_success (scorecard.py:73-91: tasks with execute run rows, role execute, executor id, task_class, merged or failed) into a private helper _class_resolved(executor_id, task_class_name, root) -> list; class_success calls it and keeps its behaviour and signature; new class_sample_size(executor_id, task_class_name, root=STATE) -> int returns len(_class_resolved(...)). jev_route.evidence_for() adds "n": class_sample_size(...) per executor.
- jev_route.adjustment(signals, evidence, eligible_ids, cfg) -> {executor_id: multiplier}. cfg [jev.routing] max_adjustment (default 0.25), evidence_floor_n (default 10). Exactly one favoured id per active branch, chosen by the same selection hypothetical() uses: branch A when max(substantial_reasoning, architectural, stronger_executor_helps) >= 0.6 -> the eligible id with the highest class_success (ties by id, ids with class_success None excluded); branch B when localized_simple >= 0.7 and elevated_risk < 0.3 -> the eligible id with the lowest expected_cost (None excluded, ties by id); branch A wins when both apply; no branch or no measurable id -> every multiplier 1.0. magnitude = max_adjustment x max(branch signal) x (confidence if confidence is not None else 0.5) x shrink, shrink = evidence_floor_n / (n_favoured + evidence_floor_n). The favoured id gets 1 + magnitude, every other eligible id gets 1.0 (never below 1 - max_adjustment, never above 1 + max_adjustment). Ids outside eligible_ids never appear; missing or malformed signals (non-numeric or outside [0, 1]) -> all 1.0.
- jev_route.active_scores(task, pool, eligible, classification, evidence, base_scores=None) -> {executor_id: base x multiplier} only when [jev.routing].mode == "active"; base_scores None -> {id: 1.0 for eligible}; shadow/off return base_scores unchanged (or that 1.0 map when None); classification None, malformed signals or empty eligible -> base_scores unchanged (baseline reproduced).
- shadow_context() keeps its shape and adds "adjustment" (computed for shadow and active) and "active": bool; the notify stub is removed; record_shadow logs adjustment and mode. No pool.toml edit; defaults in code and documented in the module docstring.
acceptance: tests/test_scorecard.py::test_class_sample_size_matches_class_success_filter — the count equals the number of resolved execute tasks class_success uses for that executor and class, and class_success's return values are unchanged

tests/test_jev_route.py::test_active_mode_adjusts_ranking_within_bounds — mode active, three eligible executors, signals favouring a stronger executor with confidence 0.9 and n 3 yield exactly one multiplier above 1.0 within [1.0, 1.25], the others 1.0, and the favoured executor's score rises relative to the rest
tests/test_jev_route.py::test_shadow_mode_never_changes_scores — mode shadow returns base_scores unchanged while shadow_context still reports the adjustment

tests/test_jev_route.py::test_extreme_probability_cannot_overturn_strong_evidence — signal 1.0 favouring executor B with n 2 against executor A with n 200, class_success 0.95 and a base score 30 percent higher leaves A ranked first

tests/test_jev_route.py::test_cold_start_default_scores_and_failure_reproduce_baseline — no evidence yields multipliers 1.0; base_scores None in active mode yields 1.0 per eligible executor before adjustment; classification None returns base_scores identical to the input
tests/test_jev_route.py::test_active_scores_never_add_ineligible_executor — an executor absent from eligible receives no score even when signals favour it

result.summary: Verified jev_route.adjustment/active_scores and scorecard._class_resolved/class_sample_size against the spec formula and all six named acceptance tests (ran them directly): magnitude/shrink/clamp math, branch-A/branch-B favoured-id selection matching hypothetical()'s tie-break, fail-open behavior for malformed/missing signals, ineligible-executor exclusion, and the shadow/active adjustment reporting all match. Ran the full test_jev_route.py (17/17 pass) and test_scorecard.py (95/95 pass individually). Running test_jev_route + test_scorecard together shows 2 unrelated failures (test_by_goal_cli_output_has_numeric_cell, test_start_forwards_scorecard_scores_to_pick_executor) from pre-existing cross-test global-state pollution; confirmed via a detached worktree at the pre-diff base commit (1ffdb17) that these same two tests fail together there too, so this is not a regression introduced by the packet.
